When the payload has no `photo` key, `toPersistence` probably maps it to `null` instead of `undefined`. Saving that null clears the photo relation. The mapper should only set null when `photo === null` was sent explicitly, and leave it `undefined` when `photo` is absent.

The photo-handling block may default `photo` to `null`, or otherwise write it, when `payload.photo` is absent. A partial update such as a first-name-only edit then sends `photo: null` to the repository. The default should be `undefined`, with null used only for an explicit `photo: null`.

The update merges the payload into the existing domain object and re-saves it through `toPersistence`. If the merge or the mapper drops the existing `photo`, the saved row loses its photo. This happens when `photo` is undefined or the spread overwrites it.

fix.description: In `toPersistence`, set `photo` to a `FileEntity` only when `domainEntity.photo` is truthy. Set it to `null` only when `domainEntity.photo === null`. Otherwise leave it `undefined` so TypeORM does not touch the column. In `UsersService.update`, initialise `photo` as `undefined` and only assign it when `payload.photo` was provided. Make the same change in the document mapper.
